title: Hybrid Rule-Learned Kernel Advisor with Safety-Fence Rollback and Customer Fingerprinting
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background:
We continue to see regression risk when the online kernel selector aggressively switches kernels during mixed prefill/decode bursts. Some customers (high-burst conversational workloads) exhibit brittle latency tails when the selector tries new microkernels without a conservative fallback. Recent incidents show 95th+ latency spikes after kernel warmstarts under mixed sequence-length distributions.

Goal:
Build a hybrid kernel advisor that combines deterministic, rule-based safety fences with a lightweight learned confidence model and a warmstart replay buffer to enable safe exploration while minimizing latency-regression exposure. Add per-customer fingerprinting so the advisor adapts to tenant workload profiles and pins safer kernel routes for critical customers.

Design highlights:
- Rule layer (safety fence): explicit rules that veto kernel switches if any hard SLO conditions are met (active tail latency > threshold, low KV-hit rate, high queue depth, or recent OOM/timeout). Rules are intentionally conservative and parameterized per deployment tier.
- Learned layer (confidence estimator): a small online model (logistic regressor) that consumes microbenchmarks + telemetry features (seqlen histogram, pref/dec ratio, KV cache hit %, recent latency residuals, occupancy estimates) and outputs a confidence score for trying a kernel. Trained initially offline from historical probes and then updated with low-rate online labels.
- Warmstart replay buffer: keep short replay buffers of representative requests and token-phase traces per customer. Before switching to a new kernel variant, run a micro-replay (synthetic prefill/decode) against the kernel in a sandbox to estimate latency/correctness impact.
- Customer fingerprinting: maintain a small fingerprint vector (categorical tags + seqlen quantiles) for customers to bias exploration schedules and prioritize stability for customers marked as high-impact.
- Rollback plan: when a kernel switch increases latency tail or error rate beyond configured deltas within a cooldown window, the safety fence triggers an immediate rollback to previous kernel and logs telemetry for analysis.

Telemetry signals used (examples):
- p95/p99 generation latency delta over 5m windows
- KV cache hit ratio (prefill cache)
- queue depth and request concurrency on target GPU pool
- microbenchmark latency distribution from warmstart replay
- correctness regressions (tokenization diffs, API-level error rates)

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No increase in p99 tail > 5% for customers in the staged canary population compared to baseline in a 2-week run.
- Successful kernel exploration that yields >= 8% average token-cost reduction for at least 3 tested mixed-burst workloads without violating latency SLOs.
- Rollback mechanism triggers properly in simulated faults (unit tests + chaos sim).

Implementation plan:
1) Define rule-set and parameters (safety thresholds) with PM and SRE (this ticket).
2) Implement lightweight confidence estimator service and feature pipeline (offline training + online update hooks).
3) Add warmstart replay harness in the sandbox runner; integrate with per-customer replay buffers.
4) Integrate advisor into routing layer with a staged rollout (alpha -> canary -> gradual ramp).
5) Observability: dashboards for exploration rate, rollback events, warmstart microbench results, per-customer exploration heatmap.

Rollout and testing:
- Alpha (internal traffic only): run advisor in dry-run mode (no actual switches) and validate score calibration against historical probes.
- Canary (5% of non-enterprise traffic, exclude high-impact flagged customers): enable advisory switching with conservative thresholds and mandatory warmstart micro-replay. Monitor for 72 hours before increasing traffic.
- Gradual ramp with automated rollback if p95 or error-rate thresholds breached.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/kernel-advisor-hybrid
- Proto PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1827
- Sandbox micro-replay harness (internal gist): https://drive.redwood.ai/replay-harness/alpha-v1

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: warmstart micro-replay may not capture all live traffic patterns. Mitigation: keep replay sampling conservative, add diversity in buffer, and rely on telemetry in first 30s after switch to trigger rollback.
- Risk: learned model miscalibration leads to over-exploration. Mitigation: keep rule-layer conservative and cap exploration rate; deploy model in staged fashion with human overrides.
- Risk: storage overhead for per-customer replay buffers. Mitigation: cap buffer size per tenant and prioritize high-impact customers for more extensive replay.

Next steps:
- Finalize safety thresholds with SRE/PM by 2026-03-05.
- Kick off implementation spike for confidence estimator (owner: @Sofia Martinez) 2026-03-09.
